reuse.why: Adds a new getExpectedScheduleAmount beside the existing shared getScheduledAmount (which the UI still uses with the old midpoint rule) and re-derives the 7.5% tolerance instead of calling getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: The API model computes expectedAmount with its own inline furthest-from-zero ternary instead of the new helper, and the tree keeps the old midpoint logic in getScheduledAmount and schedule-template, so the rule now has several divergent copies.

placement.why: The new helper sits correctly in shared/schedules.ts, but the API rule lives inline in api-models.ts rather than in the shared module.

scope.why: Edits are confined to schedule amount resolution, the API model and tests.

maintainability.why: Two parallel amount helpers with different rules, an inline API copy that ignores step 4 and approx amounts, and forecast calling without the op make the rule easy to drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal inlines its own expected-amount logic; getExpectedScheduleAmount bypasses getScheduledAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold; forecast-schedules normalizeSchedule calls it without amountOp

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount is a renamed/reshaped variant of existing getScheduledAmount, and its tolerance line restates getApproxNumberThreshold

abstraction_drift.where: New helper gains an optional amountOp with an isapprox branch; api-models.ts reimplements the rule inline, forecast-schedules omits amountOp, and getScheduledAmount/schedule-template keep the midpoint rule
